identification.summary: CybelAngel describes RuskiNet as a Russian-aligned hacktivist group that surfaced on X in February 2025 and has claimed DDoS attacks, website defacements and data leaks across more than sixteen industry sectors [S1].
identification.firstObserved: February 2025, first appearance on X per CybelAngel [S1].
identification.notes: No alternate names are stated in the sources gathered. The only source read is a single vendor blog (read via search-result summaries; the page itself could not be fetched), so every claim here rests on one secondary account [S1].

attribution.confidence: CybelAngel reports the group has not been confirmed as an APT by threat analysts, and cites Group-IB's March 2026 assessment as describing it as operating ideologically rather than as a formal arm of Russian state services; CybelAngel also says it is believed to be associated with Russian cyber operations, with attacks launched from Eastern Europe [S1].
attribution.basis: Vendor characterization only; no government attribution and no technical attribution evidence found [S1].

objectives: Disruption and publicity in support of Russian geopolitical interests through DDoS, defacement and claimed data leaks [S1].

sectors: More than sixteen industry sectors claimed [S1]
targeting.notes: These are the group's own claims as relayed by CybelAngel; none were independently verified in the sources gathered [S1].

capabilities.summary: Reported methods are DDoS, defacement, data-leak claims, and phishing and malware used to gain a foothold through social engineering [S1]. Group-IB's March 2026 assessment, as relayed by CybelAngel, rated the credibility of RuskiNet's data-leak claims at the low end of the analyst scale because several prominent leaks were recycled from earlier breaches or public sources [S1].

campaigns.name: First appearance on X
campaigns.summary: Group surfaces publicly and begins claiming DDoS, defacement and leak operations [S1].

campaigns.name: Claimed Mossad data breach
campaigns.summary: Group claimed a breach of Israel's Mossad with leaked picture IDs, names and email addresses; credibility disputed [S1].

campaigns.name: Claimed attack on KPMG Israel
campaigns.summary: Claim made during the surge of retaliation activity after Iran-related strikes (February-March 2026); verification not reported [S1].

campaigns.name: Group-IB credibility assessment
campaigns.summary: Group-IB reportedly rates RuskiNet's leak claims as low credibility [S1].

diamond.adversary: Russian-aligned hacktivist collective, not confirmed as state-directed or as an APT [S1].
diamond.capability: DDoS, defacement, phishing and malware, and leak claims of questionable authenticity [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Publicises claims via X and Telegram, with a Telegram screenshot reportedly showing an alleged attack on the Australian Department of Defence [S1].
diamond.victim: Organizations across more than sixteen sectors in the US, Canada, Israel, UK, Australia and elsewhere [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Ideological alignment with Russian geopolitical interests; activity spikes tied to events such as the 2026 Iran-related strikes [S1].
diamond.technology: Public-facing websites and services vulnerable to DDoS and defacement; users exposed to social engineering [S1].

gaps: The CybelAngel page could not be fetched; content was taken from search-result summaries and should be re-checked against the full article (English, German and French versions exist) [S1].
Publication date of the CybelAngel profile is inferred from its citation of a March 2026 Group-IB assessment; Group-IB's original report was not located.

A secondary repost (hendryadrian.com, Daily Dark Web) claims a breach of five Israeli organizations (Har Hevron Regional Council, Neot Hovav, Haruv Institute, ITIM, Moti); undated and unverified, so not used as a source.
Malpedia has an actor entry for RuskiNet but its content could not be opened.
No government advisory, MITRE group, Microsoft name, or independent technical reporting found; sponsorship, infrastructure and tooling are unknown.
Claims (Mossad, Colombia, KPMG Israel, Australian Defence) are unverified; recycled-leak assessment suggests claims may be exaggerated.

sources.title: RuskiNet: Inside a Russian-Aligned Hacktivist Group in 2026 (also 'Is RuskiNet the Next Big Russian Hacktivist Group'; date inferred from March 2026 content)

provenance.importedSummary: RuskiNet is a pro-Russian hacktivist collective associated with disruptive operations including DDoS attacks, website defacements, phishing, and data leaks against government, infrastructure, financial, and civil targets.
